newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra gets FDA nod for Pulmicort Turbuhaler.
newsitem.headline: Astra gets FDA nod for Pulmicort Turbuhaler.

text.p: Swedish drugs company Astra said Tuesday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved its anti-asthma treatment, the Pulmicort Turbuhaler.
Astra said the FDA approved the treatment for long-term use by adults and for children aged six and over. It will be introduced in the United States in the autumn.
The clinical name for the drug is budesonide inhalation powder.
"Pulmicort Turbuhaler is the first corticosteroid dry powder inhaler for asthma to be approved in the United States," Astra said in a statement.

The drug company's patented Turbuhaler delivers the substance through an inhaler without the use of propellant gases like chlorofluorocarbons, Astra said. It cited clinical tests as showing the device administers the drug more effectively than traditional aerosol inhalers.

"Pulmicort has grown to become a leading anti-asthma drug in Europe, Australia and Canada. Our intention is to make Pulmicort a leading anti-asthma medication in the United States as well," Astra CEO Hakan Mogren said in the statement.
The drug, which is now approved in 64 countries, had a 17 percent increase in sales last year to 4.73 billion crowns ($613.4 million), Astra said.
